democratic.summary: Documents support middle-class and family tax relief, targeted child and earned-income credits, higher contributions from wealthy taxpayers, estate-tax restoration, and selected corporate-rate or incentive reforms.
democratic.caveat: Positions vary by year and include both tax increases or loophole closures and targeted corporate or family tax reductions.

republican.summary: Documents support lower family, worker, investment, and corporate taxes; permanent Trump tax provisions; expanded child credits; and tax structures intended to encourage saving and business growth.
republican.caveat: Examples span broad rate cuts, targeted credits, tariff-linked predictions, and reforms whose stated economic effects were not verified.

dsa.summary: Documents support progressive income and corporate taxation, taxes on wealth, inheritances, capital gains, and financial transactions, closing corporate loopholes, and reducing regressive sales and excise taxes.
dsa.caveat: Revenue estimates and claims that particular taxes fund public programs are document assertions, not independently validated causal or fiscal findings.

democratic_vs_republican.summary: Both offer family tax relief; Democratic documents pair it with progressive taxation, while Republican documents emphasize broader rate reductions, permanence, saving, investment, and corporate competitiveness.

democratic_vs_dsa.summary: Both support more progressive taxation; DSA documents specify wealth, transaction, inheritance, and broad corporate taxes, while Democratic documents combine higher-end taxation with targeted relief.

republican_vs_dsa.summary: Republican documents seek lower investment and corporate rates; DSA documents seek higher corporate, wealth, capital-gains, inheritance, and financial-transaction taxes while reducing regressive consumption taxes.
